Although the singular center is replaced by a regular core, the stationary exterior geometry remains unchanged, demonstrating that exterior geometric observations alone cannot determine whether the black-hole interior is singular or regular. In the second approach, we modify the divergent energy-density profile and reconstruct a smooth geometry with a de Sitter core while preserving the Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter asymptotics. Regularity fixes the smoothing scale to $β=Q^2/(2m)$, leaving no independent regularization parameter. The two constructions thus provide distinct regularization mechanisms, rather than equivalent descriptions of the same spacetime.

papers.title_en: Kondo Lattice model for field induced triplet pairing in CeRh$_2$As$_2$
papers.abstract_en: Spin triplet superconductors are of interest because of their topological properties, and their robustness to high magnetic fields. CeRh$_2$As$_2$ is a unique heavy fermion superconductor with both even-parity and candidate odd-parity superconducting phases with a special feature enabling a field induced phase transition between the two. The field induced transition which switches the parity of the Cooper pairs is enabled by a staggered antisymmetric spin orbit coupling (ASOC) interaction. However, the heavy fermion origins of the superconductivity in CeRh$_2$As$_2$ and the origin of the antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling are currently unexplored. Here, we develop a Kondo lattice model for CeRh$_2$As$_2$ and demonstrate how local hybridization between Cerium $d$- and $f$-orbitals, driven by the locally broken inversion symmetry, at the Cerium sites generates the ASOC. The resulting Kondo lattice model leads to nearly degenerate even and odd parity superconducting states that display a field induced parity transition between an even-parity state and an odd-parity pseudospin triplet state. We discuss the wider implications of our results extended to other heavy fermion systems like CeSiI.

papers.title_en: Hybrid Lattice Surgery between Smooth Boundaries
papers.abstract_en: We develop smooth hybrid lattice surgery for group surface codes, enabling joint logical measurements through merge and split operations along smooth boundaries. The code patches may correspond to identical or different finite groups, including non-Abelian groups. Our central result is that smooth merge and split realize a logical $K$-coset measurement, where $K$ is the subgroup defining the interface. This generalizes the joint logical parity measurement of ordinary surface codes. Using a tensor-network representation, we derive explicit measurement circuits and develop procedures for correcting nonidentity measurement outcomes. We illustrate the framework through a generalized controlled multiplication gate between group surface codes and protocols for preparing the $T$, $CZ$, $CCX$, and $CS$ magic states, producing resources encoded in one or more $\mathbb{Z}_2$ surface code patches. Our results show how smooth hybrid lattice surgery broadens the range of logical operations available for group surface codes.

papers.title_en: Entanglement spectrum and Schmidt mode evolution during two-particle scattering
papers.abstract_en: A particle initially in a pure state but interacting with some environment evolves into a discrete ensemble of pure states, the eigenstates of its reduced density operator, with ensemble probabilities given by the corresponding eigenvalues. In this work, we use numerics to present explicit results for the time-dependence of these eigenvalues and eigenstates for simple scattering experiments in one and two dimensions. This provides a time-resolved picture of the scattering process, showing in detail how an initial state described entirely in terms of continuous parameters evolves into a discrete set of possible outcomes, each with an associated probability and time-evolving wavefunction. We find that for scattering of Gaussian wavepackets in one dimension, the late time spectrum is dominated by two large eigenvalues nearly equal to the transmission and reflection probabilities associated with the central value of momentum. The corresponding eigenstates appear as single-peaked reflected or transmitted wavepackets. The remaining smaller eigenvalues, which increase to a maximum during scattering and then decrease to small values, correspond to reflected or transmitted wavepackets with multiple spatially separated parts. In this case and also for two-dimensional scattering, we find that successively smaller eigenvalues correspond to probability distributions with successively more peaks. These multi-peaked states correspond to outcomes of the scattering experiment where a particle initially in a single wavepacket ends up in a superposition of separated wavepackets after scattering.

papers.title_en: Stability Analysis of Axion Dark Energy Model
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the stability of an axion dark energy model characterized by a periodic scalar-field potential motivated by pseudo Nambu Goldstone bosons. While such models are well suited to drive late-time cosmic acceleration and can exhibit rich dynamical features, including oscillatory behavior of the dark-energy equation-of-state parameter, their viability crucially depends on the existence of stable cosmological solutions. By reformulating the background evolution equations as an autonomous dynamical system, we identify the fixed points corresponding to radiation-dominated, matter-dominated, and dark energy dominated epochs. Using both analytical and numerical techniques, we analyze the stability properties of these fixed points within the observationally allowed region of parameter space. Our results show that the radiation- and matter-dominated phases emerge naturally as saddle points, ensuring a standard cosmological evolution, while the late-time dark energy dominated solution acts as a stable attractor. This guarantees the robustness of cosmic acceleration against variations in initial conditions. Overall, our study establishes the axion dark energy model as a dynamically consistent and observationally viable candidate for explaining the late-time accelerated expansion of the Universe.

papers.title_en: Holographic Reconstruction from Broken Conformal Gauge Symmetry
papers.abstract_en: We investigate bulk--boundary structures in $\AdS_4/\CFT_3$ from the viewpoint of gravity as a broken phase of conformal gauge symmetry. A crucial distinction is made between the Euler and Pontryagin characteristic classes. The gauge-theoretic gravitational action contains an Euler sector, whose total-derivative representation gives a boundary form depending on both intrinsic and extrinsic geometry. This structure is different from the Pontryagin descent to the three-dimensional gravitational Chern--Simons functional, whose metric variation gives the Cotton tensor and underlies the mixed boundary conditions studied by de Haro. We perform a Fefferman--Graham expansion of the Euler boundary form in asymptotically $\AdS_4$ spacetime. The normalizable coefficient $g_{(3)ij}$ does not contribute linearly to the finite Euler boundary term: its contribution from the cubic extrinsic- curvature sector vanishes by $\mathrm{Tr}\,g_{(3)}=0$, while curvature-- extrinsic-curvature terms containing $g_{(3)}$ vanish at the conformal boundary. A direct Codazzi analysis additionally shows that the Cotton tensor appears in the asymptotic mixed curvature but its contribution through the tangential-connection boundary variation vanishes for standard Dirichlet data. This indicates two distinct types of bulk--boundary structure: a global/topological Euler relation and a local Pontryagin--Cotton relation. We distinguish this kinematic Cotton appearance from a finite Cotton boundary response and discuss the implications for holographic reconstruction.

papers.title_en: New Face of Standard Model: Neutral Magnetic Monopole
papers.abstract_en: We show that the standard model has a totally new type of monopole which has the neutral magnetic charge $4π/\be$, where $\be$ is the neutral charge. This tells that the standard model has two types of monopoles, the well known Cho-Maison type which has the magnetic charge $4π/e$ and the neutral type which has the neutral magnetic charge $4π/\be$. This necessitates the new neutral charge quantization rule $\be=4πn/\bar g$, in addition to the Dirac's electric charge quantization rule $e=4πn/g$. The mass of the new monopole could be less than the Cho-Maison monopole, around 3.28 TeV. We show how to construct the neutral monopole and clarify the topological origin of the new monopole. We discuss the implications of the new monopoles in physics.

papers.title_en: Thermal and optical signatures of a magnetic AdS black hole in dark matter and quintessence
papers.abstract_en: We study a static magnetic anti-de Sitter black hole surrounded by perfect-fluid dark matter and quintessence. We follow the geometry from the horizon to the observer. We first examine the horizons and curvature. We then calculate the Hawking temperature and sparsity, weak light bending, the photon sphere, the shadow, strong-deflection coefficients, relativistic images, and simple Event Horizon Telescope size intervals. Because the model has several parameters, we use a one-dimensional benchmark path labelled by $η$. The point $η= 0$ is Schwarzschild, while $η= 1$ is the selected full configuration. This path is only a clear way to present the combined changes; it is not a new coupling. We derive the main relations step by step and test the weak- and strong-field approximations with direct numerical geodesics. Along the path, the outer horizon, photon sphere, critical shadow scale, and relativistic Einstein rings move outward. A formal solar-limb comparison gives $η\lesssim 2.06 \times 10^{-5}$ if the same local environment is placed around the Sun, but this is a source-dependent analogue rather than a universal bound. With the central mass and distance values used here, the M87* diameter allows $0 \leq η\leq 1$, while the adopted Sgr A* interval gives $η\lesssim 0.665$. Longer derivations, error propagation, and numerical checks are collected in the appendices.

papers.title_en: Rashba-controlled emergence and reversal of critical-field anisotropy in p-wave magnet--superconductor hybrids
papers.abstract_en: We show that tuning Rashba spin-orbit coupling can change the in-plane field direction along which an $s$-wave superconductor is most susceptible to Zeeman depairing. We consider a two-dimensional $s$-wave superconductor subject to an odd-parity exchange field induced by a $p$-wave magnet. Without Rashba coupling, the out-of-plane exchange field enhances the in-plane critical field but leaves its angular response exactly isotropic, despite the anisotropic magnetic spin texture. Minimizing the Bogoliubov--de Gennes grand potential over uniform singlet pairing, we find that increasing Rashba coupling first generates and then reverses the principal-axis critical-field contrast, switching the minimum-critical-field direction by $90^{\circ}$. Equal principal-axis fields at the intervening compensation point coexist with residual angular modulation. We interpret the reversal through competing momentum-dependent depairing contributions from the magnetic and Rashba spin textures, while the on-site singlet pairing channel remains unchanged. Direction-dependent discontinuous collapses of the order parameter further shape the critical-field curves. These results identify a tunable directional paramagnetic response within the uniform-pairing sector. In heterostructures with sufficient electrostatic tunability of interfacial Rashba coupling, this reversal would enable gate control of the easy-depairing axis without reorienting the magnetic texture.

papers.title_en: Data augmentation by an electro-vibratory feedback improves signal interpretation by neural networks
papers.abstract_en: Data-driven machine learning algorithms represent an alternative to numerical or analytical modeling of vibrating objects for the purpose of extracting their material or geometric properties. Their performance is conditioned by the quality of the training dataset, which should contain all possible production configurations of the object and measurement conditions. In this work, we propose a data-augmentation method based on manipulations of the vibration properties rather than numerical signal post-processing. Instead of modifying the sample’s material or geometry, we connect an additional sensor and actuator to the sample and use low-latency electronics to control the feedback signal. This delivers an electromechanical system with tunable oscillation properties. This signal diversification method is demonstrated on the classification of correct and incorrect adhesion of two aluminum plates. The labeling accuracy of 67% on nine unknown test objects, when trained on a single unchangeable training object, increases to 83% when the variety of the training vibration signals is augmented by varying the parameters of the electrovibratory feedback. This provides advantages for industrial quality control, where a large number of reference training samples are not available.

papers.title_en: u-d Quark Matter in the Enhanced pQCD Model and u-d Quark Stars in Gravity’s Rainbow
The Search for Mev-scale Neutrinos in Temporal Coincidence With o4 Gravitational Wave Events Using the Sno+ Experiment
papers.abstract_en: This dissertation presents a search for low-energy neutrinos in temporal coincidence with gravitational wave events reported by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration during the fourth observing run (O4), using 499.0 days of data collected during the liquid scintillator phase of the SNO+ experiment. The search uses inverse beta decay (IBD), which is primarily sensitive to electron antineutrinos, and neutrino-proton elastic scattering, a complementary neutral current channel providing sensitivity to all neutrino flavors. Candidate events were identified using optimized reconstruction and event-selection criteria developed with Monte Carlo simulations and validated with background-only data. The IBD background rate was measured directly from data, naturally incorporating reactor antineutrinos, geoneutrinos, radioactive backgrounds, cosmogenic backgrounds, and accidental coincidences present during detector operation. A model-independent framework was developed using flat spectrum neutrino Monte Carlo samples, allowing the detector response to be evaluated as a function of neutrino energy and applied to different theoretical emission models. As part of this work, improvements were made to the SNO+ Monte Carlo simulation, including modifications to the IBD generator to produce a true flat neutrino spectrum and corrections to the implementation of the neutrino-proton elastic scattering cross section. Detector characterization studies, including measurements of the deployed scintillator light yield and investigations of detector timing and electronics performance, were also performed to validate the detector response used throughout the analysis. The final gravitational wave-coincident dataset contained 143 candidates overlapping stable SNO+ data-taking periods. After excluding candidates classified as terrestrial or unknown by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration, the final astrophysical sample used for compact binary merger fluence limits contained 126 gravitational wave candidates. No statistically significant neutrino excess was observed in either the IBD or neutrino-proton elastic scattering channels. The IBD search observed no coincident candidates in the final astrophysical gravitational wave sample, consistent with an expected background of 1.25 ± 0.09 events. The corresponding Feldman-Cousins 90% confidence level upper limit is N90stack = 1.47 signal events. Stacked average (per gravitational wave) upper limits on the electron antineutrino fluence were derived for both monoenergetic neutrino emission and model-dependent spectra, including thermal neutrino and core-collapse supernova-inspired models used as detector sensitivity benchmarks. The neutrino-proton elastic scattering search represents the first application of this all-flavor channel to a gravitational wave-coincident neutrino search. Using an optimized ±50 s coincidence window, 108424 candidate events were observed, consistent with the expected background of 108345 ± 786 events estimated from local sidebands. The observed 0.24σ fluctuation is consistent with the background-only hypothesis. For the final astrophysical gravitational wave sample, the Feldman-Cousins method gives a 90% confidence level upper limit of N90stack = 1479.6 signal events. These results are used to derive the first all-flavor neutrino-proton elastic scattering fluence limits associated with compact binary merger candidates. The resulting SNO+ IBD fluence limits improve upon previous liquid scintillator gravitational wave-neutrino searches by approximately an order of magnitude in the few-MeV energy region, primarily due to the larger fiducial target mass, increased gravitational wave sample size, and low background rate achieved in SNO+. The neutrino-proton elastic scattering results establish the first all-flavor MeV neutrino search through this interaction channel in coincidence with gravitational wave events. Together, these analyses extend previous multi-messenger searches performed by Borexino, KamLAND, and Super-Kamiokande and demonstrate the capability of SNO+ to search for weak neutrino signals associated with astrophysical transients.

papers.title_en: ESC Enables Protection of an Accelerator Superconducting Magnet With $>$5 kA/mm$^{2}$ Copper Current Density
papers.abstract_en: A new quench-protection technique, energy shift with coupling (ESC), has recently been proposed and shows significant promise for the protection of high-field magnets. The ESC system includes normal-conducting coils that are strongly magnetically coupled to, but galvanically insulated from, the magnet coils. When activated, the system rapidly transfers energy from the magnet to the ESC coils, substantially reducing ohmic losses at the magnet hot spot and promoting the transition of the superconducting coils to the normal state through transient losses. During the subsequent magnet-current discharge, part of the stored magnetic energy is transferred to the ESC coils. ESC was recently demonstrated successfully at CERN on a 400 mm long flat racetrack magnet structure without an aperture. In this work, we present the application of the ESC method to a subscale common-coil magnet known as the subscale stress-managed common-coil series (subSMCC2), designed and manufactured by the Magnet Development Laboratory at the Paul Scherrer Institute. The subSMCC2 is a 300 mm long magnet comprising four stress-managed Nb₃Sn common coils and is designed to reach bore and peak coil fields of approximately 5.3 T and 6.4 T, respectively, at a short-sample current of 9.5 kA. Protecting this magnet following a quench, without the use of energy extraction, is particularly challenging because of its very high stabilizer current density, exceeding 5 kA/mm². The proposed ESC-based protection scheme employs two common-coil-type ESC coils made from rectangular copper conductors and located on the outer sides of the magnet coils. Tests performed at the CERN magnet test facility successfully demonstrated the performance of the ESC system under a variety of operating conditions. These results show that ESC is an effective, high-performance quench-protection technology capable of protecting magnets operating at very high current densities.

papers.title_en: Quantum Key Distribution Network Simulator With Hyperparameter Tuning for Realistic Performance Analysis
papers.abstract_en: Realistic simulation of quantum key distribution (QKD) networks requires a combination of precise models of quantum channels and network functions. Unfortunately, existing QKD network simulators lack either rigorous quantum physics modeling or network key-management and routing protocols, which limit their practical applicability. To address this limitation, we propose a QKD network simulator with hyperparameter tuning (QKDSim-HT), a NetSquid-based simulator specialized for polarization-based discrete-variable QKD networks. Specifically, QKDSim-HT models properties in quantum physics (photon loss, polarization-dependent depolarization, detector inefficiencies, dark counts, and dead times) as well as advanced functionalities in networking algorithms (multi-hop key relay and adaptive routing). Extensive simulations over diverse topologies reveal that the networking performance varied with respect to the fundamental properties of quantum physics, such as depolarization, fiber length, and channel attenuation. As a representative use case of QKDSim-HT, simulation results from QKDSim-HT over simple examples clearly manifest that a design of QKD networks highly affects performance of the networks. Accordingly, QKDSim-HT can serve as a practical platform for performance evaluation and optimization of quantum secured network.

papers.title_en: Suppression of two-stream and Weibel instabilities in ultra-relativistic electron–positron plasma
papers.abstract_en: We present a unified theoretical framework for analyzing both electrostatic two-stream and electromagnetic Weibel instabilities in counterstreaming electron-positron pair plasmas. Through systematic derivation of dispersion relations in non-relativistic and relativistic regimes, we demonstrate how the symmetric mass ratio fundamentally alters instability characteristics compared to electron-ion systems. The two-stream instability, driven by longitudinal electrostatic perturbations parallel to beam motion, exhibits enhanced growth rates in pair plasmas due to equal contributions from both species, with relativistic suppression scaling as γ0−3 for both electrons and positrons. The Weibel instability, arising from transverse electromagnetic modes perpendicular to streaming directions, lacks the heavy-ion stabilization present in electron-ion plasmas, producing broader unstable spectral ranges and modified saturation levels. We derive explicit conditions determining the relative dominance of each mechanism across parameter space defined by drift velocity, wavenumber orientation, and relativistic Lorentz factor. Our analysis shows that longitudinal two-stream modes dominate at small perpendicular wavenumbers and moderate drift velocities, while transverse Weibel modes become prevalent at high perpendicular wavenumbers and large velocity spreads or temperature anisotropies. These findings have direct implications for understanding magnetic field generation, particle acceleration, and energy dissipation in astrophysical pair plasmas including pulsar wind nebulae, gamma-ray burst internal shocks, and active galactic nuclei jets where counterstreaming pair populations naturally arise.

papers.title_en: Developing and validating models of open quantum systems in solid-state nanostructures
papers.abstract_en: Realistic quantum devices are open systems, and their behaviour depends not only on the subsystem of interest but also on how the environment is modelled and how the relevant observables are extracted. This thesis studies that problem in three settings. First, we study cavity-assisted qubit readout beyond the dispersive regime. We show that once coherent excitation exchange and dissipation become relevant, a microscopic treatment is needed to describe the readout quantitatively, and the optimal readout is set by a trade-off between signal accumulation and the distinguishability of the readout states. Second, we compare fermionic and spin baths in non-interacting transport models and show that spin baths reproduce fermionic reduced dynamics only in the large-bath weak-coupling limit, while clear deviations appear for smaller baths and near half-filling. Third, we study charge transport in molecular junctions using Automated Compression of Environments (ACE). There, the main difficulty is not the time evolution itself, but the extraction of the transport current, since this observable depends on system-environment correlations and is therefore not contained in the reduced system density matrix alone. We show that a probe-mode construction provides a viable route to reformulate the current as a system observable. This thesis advances our understanding of what is required for accurate modelling of open quantum dynamics across a range of solid-state settings, from cavity-assisted qubit readout to charge transport in molecular junctions.

papers.title_en: Using Printed Circuit Boards and MOSFET Switch Arrays Toward the Reliable Manufacture of Superconducting Rectifiers
papers.abstract_en: Using superconducting rectifiers to energize high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets is a promising approach to accelerate the uptake of HTS magnet technology. In this work, we start to address two limitations of the HTS superconducting rectifier concepts published to date; their low magnet charging voltages, and the variable properties of their HTS-based switches. Our approach is to test a centre-tapped full-wave transformer–rectifier utilizing HTS secondary windings and switch-arrays of Si <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mosfet</small>s mounted on a printed-circuit board (PCB). This approach has the advantage of greatly facilitating reproducible and reliable manufacture. The rectifier demonstrated magnet charging voltages exceeding a cycle-averaged 80 mV at 100 A and with typically more than 30% of the power supplied to the primary coils delivered to the magnet. We found it to be resilient to our preliminary thermal-cycling testing, with no degradation in performance observed over eight liquid-nitrogen to ambient (77–295 K) thermal cycles. We compare the impact of voltage- and current-controlled modes for the rectifier’s power supply. Our conclusion is that superconducting rectifiers using <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mosfet</small> switch arrays placed on PCBs is a very promising approach for low-current HTS magnet power supplies.

papers.title_en: Compact High Turns Ratio Superconducting Transformer: Comparison Between Cu and REBCO Winding Materials
papers.abstract_en: Compact high turns ratio superconducting transformers are used to transfer power between low-current copper/ semiconductor-based circuits and high-current superconductor-based circuits. This type of transformer is a key component in devices, such as superconducting transformer rectifiers and superconducting current source inverters. Typically the copper winding and the superconducting winding are arranged with a turn ratio above 100:1, respectively, and are situated entirely within a cryogenic environment. The ohmic losses associated with the high count copper winding is problematic for most cryogenic applications and demands attention even when low currents on the order of 1–10 A are used. To address this problem, a transformer has been made using rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) high-temperature superconductor (HTS) coated conductor for both the primary and secondary windings. The coupling coefficient and power consumption of this transformer were measured and compared to an equivalent transformer consisting of a copper primary winding and HTS secondary winding. The HTS primary was found to provide a significant reduction in transformer power consumption and a slight improvement to transformer coupling at frequencies below <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>8 Hz. An increased transformer core loss and winding AC loss began to negate these efficiency improvements above <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>8 Hz. In addition, cowinding the primary and secondary windings provided a higher coupling coefficient and lower power consumption for all winding combinations and frequencies tested. Finally, a short discussion on the implications of these findings respect to superconducting transformer rectifiers contextualizes the findings.

papers.title_en: The Primary Interaction Compton Couple algorithm for sorting GRETINA/GRETA interaction points
Alfvénicity and proximity to parallel-mode marginal stability in the slow solar wind
Mechanical Characteristics of Aluminium-Stabilized Stacked REBCO Tape Cable for the CEPC Detector Magnet
papers.abstract_en: This article investigates the mechanical characteristics and critical current performance of aluminum-stabilized stacked REBCO tape cable (ASTC) for the circular electron-positron collider detector magnet. In-plane bending, torsion, and uniaxial tension tests are carried out, combined by finite element analysis. The correlation between critical current and strain under different loading conditions is systematically analyzed, and key mechanical thresholds are determined. Results show that the minimum allowable in-plane bending diameter is 1200 mm. The critical twist pitch is 327 mm. The critical current degrades to 95% of the initial value when the tensile strain in the REBCO tape reaches 0.37%. This study provides essential experimental data and theoretical support for the structural design and engineering application of ASTC in high-field superconducting magnets.

papers.title_en: Designing Josephson Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers: EM-Circuit Cosimulation and Experimental Validation
papers.abstract_en: The development of large-scale superconducting quantum computers critically depends on the accurate readout of qubit states. To enable this, cryogenic parametric amplifiers have been proposed and developed, and have since found widespread use in small-signal detection applications. Among various amplifier architectures, Josephson traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (JTWPAs) are widely adopted due to their broad bandwidth, high saturation power, and compatibility with superconducting qubits. In this work, we present a design workflow of JTWPAs based on a cosimulation approach combining electromagnetic (EM) and circuit-level simulation. We apply this method to a uniform JTWPA, comparing our simulation results with experimental data. To mitigate the challenge of constructing lumped-element circuit models usually used in the conventional simulation method, we directly perform full EM analysis of the device to accurately determine its linear response. The extracted S-parameters are then fed into a nonlinear harmonic balance simulator with Josephson junctions modeled as circuit elements. By doing so, the linear and gain properties of the JTWPA are extracted. Different factors that impact device performance including gain compression, phase matching, and fabrication imperfections are further investigated and modeled. A good agreement between simulation and measurements is identified, establishing the effectiveness of our approach in designing quantum parametric amplifiers.

papers.title_en: Mathematics of effective q-plate in polarization optics
papers.abstract_en: The q-plate is a spatially inhomogeneous SU(2) birefringent optical element that has garnered significant interest due to its ability to mediate the spin-orbit interaction of light and facilitate the generation of structured light with singularities. The q-plate features a spatially varying fast axis orientation defined by three parameters: the topological charge q, retardance delta, and the offset angle $alpha_0$. While the parameter alpha_0 can be changed many times by rotation, any change in the charge and/or retardance entails the fabrication of a new plate. This limitation can be overcome through the concept of an effective waveplate, where multiple waveplates, homogeneous or inhomogeneous, are aligned coaxially so that, under specific constraints, the composite system emulates the behavior of a single effective waveplate. This work presents a comprehensive mathematical formalism for realizing an effective waveplate through a cascaded configuration of three q-plates, each chosen as either a quarter-wave q-plate, a half-wave q-plate, or a combination thereof. Some configurations offer tunability of the retardance over the full range from 0 to $2pi$, even though q-plates with fixed retardances of $pi/2$ and pi are used in sequence to form an effective q-plate. This feature enables holonomic polarization walk on the higher-order Poincare sphere. Such a capability holds significant potential for applications involving structured light associated with the higher-order Poincare sphere, particularly in controlled polarization transformations and polarization-topology engineering.

papers.title_en: Bayesian vs Deep learning: Parameter constraints for an anisotropic universe in f(Q) gravity
Quantum at the Edge: Scalable Standalone FPGA Emulator for QAOA-Based Weighted-MaxCut
papers.abstract_en: Quantum computing (QC) emulation is critical for exploring and advancing near-term quantum algorithms, given the ongoing scalability and reliability challenges of quantum hardware. While FPGA-based QC emulators have emerged as efficient alternatives to bridge the gap toward practical quantum computers, most existing solutions depend on high-performance systems, limiting their applicability in embedded and edge environments. In this work, we present a scalable, standalone FPGA-based emulator specialized for resource-constrained systems. Our design targets the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), particularly for the Weighted-MaxCut problem. By leveraging diagonal decomposition and a pipeline-centric hardware architecture, we reduce the computational complexity of QAOA from $\boldsymbol{O(N^{2})}$ to $\boldsymbol{O(N)}$, where $\boldsymbol{N}$ $\boldsymbol{=}$ $\boldsymbol{2^{n}}$ is the state dimension for $\boldsymbol{n}$ qubits. This reformulation and its architectural co-design significantly reduces hardware overhead, enabling larger qubit configurations on edge-level FPGAs. We encapsulate these optimizations into a hardware accelerator called the Quantum MaxCut Accelerator (QMA), which integrates seamlessly into a RISC-V platform, forming a self-contained emulator. Additionally, we introduce QC Emulator eXpress (QEX), a full-stack automation framework that streamlines QMA integration into configurable RISC-V platforms, significantly facilitating rapid and scalable emulator development and deployment. Through extensive prototyping of various QAOA emulators, our experiments confirm that the proposed QMA achieves energy reductions of up to $\textbf{907}\boldsymbol{\times}$ compared to the CPU-only software baseline under the same standalone FPGA/RISC-V setting and reliably supports up to 9 qubits on a mid-tier FPGA. These results demonstrate the energy efficiency and scalability of the proposed system as a self-contained FPGA/RISC-V platform for edge-local QAOA emulation, prototyping, and HW/SW co-design exploration under resource-constrained conditions.

papers.title_en: Theory of double flat-top solitons in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract_en: Solitons are fundamental entities in nonlinear wave equations across diverse branches of physics. In systems with competing nonlinearities, a hallmark transition occurs from traditional bell-shaped profiles to flat-top configurations as the norm increases. In this work, we analyze double flat-top solitons in systems of two coupled generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equations. We develop a theoretical and variational framework that provides both physical insight and a computationally efficient description of these eigenstates. In the large-norm regime, and for a broad class of nonlinear potentials supporting flat-top states, we derive explicit analytical expressions for the plateau densities and chemical potentials, together with variational estimates for the interfacial properties characterizing the solutions. These quantities are controlled by algebraic conditions that generalize the Maxwell coexistence condition to coupled wave functions. We show that two-component flat-top solitons may form core–shell configurations, in which a two-component core is surrounded by a shell of the dominant species, as well as no-shell configurations, where both species occupy the same spatial domain. Using the cubic-quintic nonlinearity as a prototypical model, we compare these analytical predictions with direct numerical computations of the stationary states and find excellent agreement in the flat-top regime. The resulting picture admits a natural interpretation in terms of phase coexistence in an effective binary fluid, with kink-like interfaces carrying an excess grand potential that plays the role of a surface tension. This formalism is applicable to diverse physical platforms, including nonlinear optics, multicomponent Bose–Einstein condensates, and Q-ball configurations in relativistic field theories.

Rotating black holes in perfect fluid dark matter: Horizons, photon orbits, and shadows
papers.abstract_en: We investigate rotating black holes surrounded by perfect-fluid dark matter (PFDM), described by the parameter k, and determine the Kerr-connected region of the (a/M, k/M) parameter space that contains an event horizon. The critical value kc(a), obtained from the degenerate-horizon conditions <math altimg="si22.svg"><mrow><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Δ</mi></mstyle><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><msup><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Δ</mi></mstyle><mo>′</mo></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, defines the boundary between black-hole and horizonless configurations. We derive an exact parametric form of this extremal boundary and show that its near-Kerr behavior includes a logarithmic correction; therefore, <math altimg="si23.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>≃</mo><mn>2.8828</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo linebreak="badbreak">−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo linebreak="badbreak">/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mrow><mn>1.5377</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is only an empirical fit over 0.90 ≤ a/M ≤ 0.999, not an asymptotic scaling law. For horizon-bearing solutions, we calculate unstable spherical photon orbits and the shadow’s mean radius, area, and distortion, finding that increasing k/M shifts the photon region inward and reduces the shadow size. Backward ray tracing through a phenomenological optically thin disk, tested on independent 41<sup loc="post">2</sup>, 81<sup loc="post">2</sup>, and 161<sup loc="post">2</sup> image grids, confirms this trend: for <math altimg="si6.svg"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow></math> and an inclination of 17<sup loc="post">∘</sup>, the 20 μas beam-convolved ridge diameter decreases from 42.47 to 37.88 μas as k/M increases from 0 to 0.08, with the two finest grids agreeing to within 0.5%. Thus, PFDM produces a consistent contraction from the horizon and photon region to the geometric shadow and image ridge, although these illustrative images do not provide an Event Horizon Telescope constraint because they lack a self-consistent emission model and interferometric likelihood analysis.

papers.title_en: The investigation of various gravitational soliton profiles for Einstein’s vacuum field equations under the unified Hirota bilinear approach
papers.abstract_en: Einstein’s vacuum field equation (EVFE) occupies a central position in general relativity, governing the geometry of spacetime in regions free from matter sources. The nonlinear PDE analyzed here is a specific (1+1)-dimensional reduction of the full vacuum field equations, obtained by imposing the Guilfoyle metric ansatz and setting <math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3328"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>; all results pertain to this reduced model. Despite its physical importance, the catalogue of exact nonlinear wave solutions for this reduced EVFE does not yet include spatially localized multi-component and breather-type structures: no such solutions have been constructed for this equation prior to this work. We address this gap by applying the Hirota bilinear method with strategically chosen polynomial test functions to obtain, within a single unified framework, an extensive family of exact analytic solutions: lump, lump 1-stripe, lump 2-stripe, lump-periodic, manifold periodic, rogue wave, Ma breather, Kuznetsov–Ma breather, generalized breather, Akhmediev breather, and the corresponding standard rogue wave. We further construct interaction solutions among lump, periodic, and kink-wave components and illustrate their three-scale spatial structure through contour analysis. Three-dimensional surface profiles and contour maps are generated for each solution class with systematic parameter variation, revealing how background level, wavenumber, and velocity parameters control the localization geometry, peak amplitude, and propagation direction. The solutions carry direct relevance to gravitational wave physics, nonlinear optics, and ocean wave dynamics, and provide benchmark configurations for numerical relativity and wave-scattering studies.

papers.title_en: Hardware-Friendly Estimation of LCU-Based Expectation Values via Quantum-to-Classical Workload Shifting
papers.abstract_en: Estimating the expectation value of an observable $O$ for a quantum state evolved under a general, possibly non-unitary, operator $A$ is a fundamental task in quantum simulation, chemistry, and variational algorithms. Existing linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) approaches implement $A$ on hardware, requiring ancilla qubits, controlled unitaries and, in randomized variants, fresh circuit executions for every Monte Carlo sample. These costs are prohibitive on NISQ and early fault-tolerant devices. We propose HERMES (Hardware-Efficient Reusable Measurements for Estimating LCU-based expectation valueS), which moves the processing of $A$ entirely to the classical domain. Expanding $A$ and $O$ in the Pauli basis and sampling pairs of Pauli terms classically, HERMES rewrites $μ= \mathrm{Tr}(OAρA^{\dagger})/\mathrm{Tr}(AρA^{\dagger})$ as a ratio of weighted sums of Pauli expectation values on the unmodified state $ρ$, with no ancillas, controlled unitaries, or quantum implementation of $A$. A two-level measurement reduction scheme (Pauli deduplication and commuting-group partitioning) bounds the number of distinct measurement settings independently of the sample count, unlike randomized LCU methods whose circuit executions grow linearly with it. On ground-state energy estimation of $\mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{LiH}$ via imaginary-time evolution, HERMES matches or beats Pauli single-ancilla LCU baseline using shallow circuits with no two-qubit gates beyond state preparation under qubit-wise commuting grouping. It is also more robust to noise and completes a noisy $\mathrm{LiH}$ simulation infeasible for the baseline, at the cost of classical overhead growing with the number of Pauli terms in $A$.

papers.title_en: Additive uncertainty relations via pseudospectral methods
papers.abstract_en: Given Hermitian observable $A$, the variance of $A$ is given by the difference of expectations $\langle A^2\rangle - \langle A\rangle^2$, where the expectation of an observable implicitly assumes a choice of state for the underlying system. As a sub-case of a general lower bound for the sum of variances for finitely many arbitrary elements in a $C^*$-algebra, we prove that the sum of the variances for $d$ observables $A_1, \dots , A_d$ is greater than some expression in the expectations $\langle i[A_j,A_k]\rangle$ for $j\neq k$ plus the square of the smallest singular value of the associated localizer. In special cases, this expression is just a root mean square average. Our technique also derives a general containment between the Clifford pseudospectra and quadratic pseudospectra for $d$ observables.

papers.title_en: Performing a Quantum Subroutine Using Cluster States
papers.abstract_en: Quantum subroutines, like their classical counterparts, serve as essential components of larger algorithms. They can be realized using gate based architectures or measurement based quantum computation (MBQC), where computation proceeds through adaptive measurements on highly entangled cluster states. In this work, we implement a phase oracle as a reusable subroutine within the MBQC framework using experimentally feasible cluster states. Unlike prior demonstrations of Grover's algorithm in MBQC that omit explicit oracle construction, our approach provides a transparent formulation of the oracle subroutine, including its measurement patterns, byproduct correlations, density-matrix simulations, and corresponding MBQC measurement circuits.

papers.title_en: An Invitation to Algebraic Methods in Quantum Theory
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we present various well-studied examples of quantum systems, and discuss how they might be analysed algebraically. We analyse the harmonic oscillator, hydrogenic atom, optical components, and particle spin using multiple algebraic methods, and highlight the central importance of algebraic relationships between operators in determining the physical character of the system. In particular, we show: the ubiquity of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)\cong\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ as the ``spectrum generating algebra''; the role of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ in determining the action of optical components; that an elementary algebraic approach to particle spin offers novel insights into its nature versus the usual approaches; and how understanding the full (often hidden) symmetry of a problem enables it to be solved immediately without the need to solve differential equations. We hope this work will serve as a gentle introduction to algebraic methods in quantum mechanics for the interested reader --- we therefore signpost active areas of research within the community.

papers.title_en: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
papers.abstract_en: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincaré method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.

papers.title_en: Real-space construction and selection rules of center-of-mass momentum eigenstates in two-dimensional many-body lattices
papers.abstract_en: We present a comprehensive framework for the real-space construction of center-of-mass (c.m.) momentum eigenstates in two-dimensional (2D) quantum many-body systems. Unlike standard momentum-space approaches, our real-space formalism explicitly captures the non-uniformity of cyclic subspace dimensions, which are fundamentally governed by the spatial symmetries of the many-body configurations and particle statistics. We demonstrate that performing 2D real-space translations on multi-particle states naturally induces non-trivial translation phase factors associated with the characters of these stabilizer subgroups, leading to a renormalization of permissible momentum values. Notably, we identify an anomalous cross-dimensional momentum coupling in highly symmetric particle distributions, where the permissible momentum values in one direction are strictly constrained by those in the perpendicular direction. We emphasize the algorithmic necessity of this coupling, as neglecting it leads to missing or duplicated basis states in numerical implementations. Concrete examples are provided to demonstrate the practical implementation and physical consequences of this framework.

papers.title_en: Prediction of the Geoneutrino Signal at the Jinping Neutrino Experiment
papers.abstract_en: We present refined predictions of the geoneutrino flux for the 500-tonne Jinping Neutrino Experiment (JNE). We construct a local crustal model with a resolution of \(0.2^\circ\times0.2^\circ\) based on the SWChinaCVM-2.0 seismic velocity model and integrate it with CRUST1.0 to establish our reference model. For comparison, we also calculate the geoneutrino flux using ECM1 and CRUST1.0 as standalone global crustal models. Assuming an energy scale of 500~p.e./MeV and an exposure of 500~t$\times$1500~days, we predict the inverse beta decay event spectrum, including both the geoneutrino signal and the reactor antineutrino background. The distinct spectral shapes of the $^{238}$U, $^{232}$Th, and reactor antineutrino components allow their respective contributions to be obtained through spectral fitting. These predictions provide inputs for the JNE data analysis, particularly for extracting the mantle geoneutrino signal and testing competing bulk silicate Earth models.

papers.title_en: Single-step SU(3) Hahn Echo in a Qutrit Atom Interferometer
papers.abstract_en: The Hahn echo is a well-known dynamical decoupling method that refocuses the dephasing due to energy inhomogeneities of a spin-1/2 ensemble and is widely used to extend phase coherence in quantum computers and sensors. Extensions of such techniques beyond the spin-1/2 have been reported, but have mainly used SU(2) gates, limiting their scalability. Here, we generalize the Hahn echo to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates and extend the coherence time by more than an order of magnitude. The gates are generated through optimal control theory and implemented in an ultracold atomic ensemble in free fall. A quantum process tomography procedure benchmarks the gates and yields fidelities of ~ 93%, limited mainly by state preparation and measurement errors. Due to the geometry of the laser beams, the generalized Hahn echo also realizes a three-path Mach-Zehnder atomic interferometer with two independent interferometric phase differences. Our results therefore establish SU(3) control for dynamical decoupling of qutrits and multi-path atom interferometers, with the latter opening the possibility for vector force measurements and interferometric tests of the validity of Born's rule.

papers.title_en: Near-field maps of topological edge states of molecular aggregates
papers.abstract_en: Self-assembled two-dimensional molecular aggregates provide a versatile platform for engineering excitonic states, including topologically nontrivial edge states. However, these edge-states are difficult to probe optically: they have weak far-field transition strengths, and far-field spectra do not reveal whether an excitation is localized at the edge. For an aggregate consisting of two sublattices of molecules with genuinely complex transition dipoles, we show that spatially resolved near-field spectroscopy encodes the full spatial structure of these states. The resulting near-field maps do not mirror the site populations, but instead exhibit strongly nonuniform, interference-like features. We demonstrate that a convolutional neural network can reconstruct the complex expansion coefficients of the eigenstates from these maps, and that this reconstruction is robust against substantial random noise.

papers.title_en: High Resolution Hyperspectral Quantum Infrared Imaging with Undetected Photons
papers.abstract_en: Quantum sensing in the infrared regime often demands the use of expensive and cryogenically operated detectors. Nonlinear interferometry has paved the way for information transfer from the infrared to the near--infrared or visible regime in various quantum technologies. A particularly interesting application of these interferometers involves spectrally--resolved quantum imaging using undetected photons, enabled by the use of temperature--tunable parametric amplifiers. In this work, we demonstrate spectrally resolved transmission imaging with undetected photons around 1550 nm using a spontaneous parametric down conversion based folded nonlinear interferometric scheme, registering the attenuation of a zebrafish larva as a biological feasibility test. We characterize and calibrate the interferometer, having achieved spectrally resolved interference fringes with a maximum baseline visibility of $\sim 74\%$ in the near--infrared regime. Phase--stepped readout of a grating spectrometer gives a resolving power of $\sim1460$ (from the spectrometer's point spread function) at 1550 nm, and $\sim 730$ from the coherence length, the finest reported for imaging with undetected photons, over an instantaneous spectral window of $\approx 51$ cm$^{-1}$.

papers.title_en: Asymptotic scars arising from the remnants of quantum phase transitions
papers.abstract_en: Many-body localisation, Hilbert space fragmentation and quantum many-body scars (QMBS) are well-established mechanisms of ergodicity breaking in quantum systems. Recently, asymptotic quantum many-body scars (AQMBS), non-thermal states whose stability grows with system size, have been proposed theoretically and probed experimentally. Here, we show that AQMBS arise naturally as remnants of certain quantum phase transitions. For a broad class of frustration-free Hamiltonians, we prove that their gapless excitations survive deformation into a scarred Hamiltonian as states whose energy variance is bounded by the excitation gap. Consequently, the gapless excitations at a quantum critical point become AQMBS of the scarred Hamiltonian. Their fidelity relaxation time is then set by the critical scaling of the gap, determined by the dynamic critical exponent. Modelling the critical Fredkin and Motzkin chains and the two-dimensional PVBS model, we obtain AQMBS whose variances directly reflect the dynamic exponents of the underlying transitions. Where the gap of the Motzkin chain closes super-exponentially, we find exponentially stable AQMBS, for which we also observe numerical evidence of volume-law entanglement.

papers.title_en: Robustness of Quantum Correlations and Controlled Teleportation Fidelity under Noisy Channels
papers.abstract_en: In distributed quantum computing, quantum networks provide a potential infrastructure for long-range quantum information processing. Controlled quantum teleportation (CQT) is a key practically relevant protocol that can connect two parties on a network and enables a third party, the controller to allow or abort the secure teleportation of an arbitrary single-qubit state between the two parties. We investigate the robustness of a three-qubit GHZ resource under bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise. Using the Kraus-operator formalism, we characterize the noisy resource through multipartite quantum discord, genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC), localizable entanglement (LE), and CQT fidelity. We also outline a proof-of-concept photonic implementation for preparing the three-qubit GHZ resource and realizing the CQT protocol, which could enable experimental investigation of the effects of noise. Our results show that bit-flip and amplitude-damping noise generally preserve useful mutipartite quantum correlations over broader noise parameter ranges. Interestingly, multipartite discord exhibits freezing under bit-flip noise over a finite parameter regime. Moreover, discord can persist beyond the sudden death of genuine multipartite entanglement, revealing the distinct robustness of nonclassical correlations. We further demonstrate that CQT fidelity which characterizes the performance of CQT can exceed the classical threshold even after GMC vanishes, while LE more closely reflects the operational usefulness of the noisy resource. These findings highlight the complementary roles of quantum correlations and entanglement in assessing the resilience of GHZ-based protocols.

papers.title_en: Material criteria for angular-momentum transfer from twisted photons to photoelectrons
papers.abstract_en: We study the material requirements for transferring the total-angular-momentum (TAM) projection of a twisted photon to the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a photoelectron emitted from an $n$-type semiconductor surface. Within a single-valley effective-mass model of surface photoemission, we calculate OAM-resolved spectra for GaAs, InSb, $\mathrm{InAs}_{0.34}\mathrm{Sb}_{0.66}$, and $\mathrm{Hg}_{0.76}\mathrm{Cd}_{0.24}\mathrm{Te}$ irradiated by twisted photons with Laguerre--Gaussian--like momentum profile. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. Efficient transfer requires the transverse momentum of the conduction electron to be much smaller than the transverse momentum width of the photon, which favors low temperatures, small conduction-band effective masses, and shallow donor levels. GaAs is less favorable within the present model because of its larger effective mass and deeper donor levels. We also discuss the demanding photon-wave packet parameters, possible extensions to Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and post-emission OAM selection. Although the generation of vortex electrons with a vanishing OAM uncertainty via photoemission seems challenging, we argue that it is still possible to generate single-electron vortex states with a finite OAM dispersion.

papers.title_en: Coherent axion electrodynamics in OSIRIS: a counter-propagating axion-photon parametric instability
papers.abstract_en: We present a coherent axion-electrodynamics extension of the OSIRIS particle-in-cell code and use it to identify and benchmark a parametric axion-photon instability supported by two equal counter-propagating electromagnetic pumps. The module evolves a cell-centered axion field together with a separately stored first-order electromagnetic response on the native staggered OSIRIS grid. Re-examining the previously proposed strictly co-linear branch shows that it is removed when the axion-Maxwell equations are reduced consistently. A closely related standing-wave geometry, however, supports a distinct Floquet instability. We derive the coupled Floquet problem for an equal-amplitude counter-propagating pump pair and obtain a reduced analytic growth rate and cutoff for the dominant long-wavelength envelope branch. For an axion mass-to-pump-frequency ratio of 0.06 and a per-beam vector-potential amplitude of 0.3, simulations at coupling strengths of 0.60, 0.80, and 1.00 reproduce both the growth-rate spectrum and the coupling-dependent instability boundary. The reduced theory predicts envelope-mode cutoffs of 8.44, 10.80, and 13.23, while OSIRIS finds exponential growth through modes 8, 10, and 13, respectively, with the next resolved modes stable. The electromagnetic diagnostics additionally resolve exponentially growing sidebands at twice the pump wavenumber, while the zero-wavenumber electric component exhibits no sustained growth, as expected for the unstable Floquet eigenvector. The agreement provides an end-to-end benchmark of the coherent axion-electromagnetic coupling and demonstrates that parametric growth of the axion field is present in a two-beam pump geometry.

papers.title_en: Bayesian analysis of the Coulomb breakup of C19
papers.abstract_en: Coulomb breakup is a common experimental technique to study the structure of halo nuclei. Coupling a halo effective field theory (Halo-EFT) description of these nuclei to accurate reaction models provides an ideal tool to analyze such experiments. In particular, it enables us to sample the space of the low-energy constants of this EFT within a Bayesian approach. This allows us to infer nuclear-structure information from the reaction data in a systematic and reliable way. Moreover, it provides an estimate of the uncertainty on those structure observables. We apply this to re-analyze the Coulomb breakup of $^{19}$C measured on Pb at 67 MeV/nucleon in RIKEN [T. Nakamura et al. Phys. Rev. Lett. 83, 1112 (1999)]. We obtain a new and more accurate value for the one-neutron separation energy $S_n(^{19}\mathrm{C}) = 0.60 \pm 0.02$ MeV and an improved estimate of the asymptotic normalization constant of its bound state $C_{1/2^+} = 0.85 \pm 0.02$ fm$^{-1/2}$. In addition, we estimate the uncertainty related to other model inputs at about 15% on both structure observables.

papers.title_en: Bogoliubov Dynamics and Zitterbewegung in Optical Dirac Systems
papers.abstract_en: We develop a bosonic Bogoliubov description of Zitterbewegung in time-dependent optical-Dirac systems. Within the optical-Dirac framework, the anomalous pair-creation and pair-annihilation terms of a bosonic Bogoliubov Hamiltonian correspond to couplings between the positive- and negative-frequency sectors, whose coherence underlies the Zitterbewegung response. When the constitutive parameters vary in time, the resulting moving-frame connection generates dynamical interbranch coupling and positive--negative-frequency coherence. Under periodic modulation, this coupling becomes resonant near $Ω\simeq2ω_0$, leading to parametric amplification of the coherence and consequently to an enhanced Zitterbewegung motion.

papers.title_en: Quantum Landau Lifshitz Gilbert equation in ferromagnetic conductors and magnetic insulators
papers.abstract_en: Understanding the microscopic origin of magnetic damping is essential for describing magnetization dynamics in nanoscale magnetic systems. In this work, we develop a microscopic framework to derive Gilbert damping terms from specific interactions in ferromagnetic conductors and magnetic insulators. In ferromagnetic conductors, magnetic damping is dominated by the s d exchange interaction between the localized magnetic moments and the itinerant electrons, which is effectively equivalent to an electronmagnon interaction. From the spin diffusion equation and the spin transfer torque therein, we obtain the corresponding quantum LLG equation. In magnetic insulators, where free electrons are absent, spin phonon interactions become the primary source of the damping.Starting from an effective spin phonon interaction and using linear response theory, we derive a quantum LLG equation with a Gilbert damping tensor analytically. Our results demonstrate that different microscopic interactions lead to qualitatively different structures of magnetic damping. Instead of being described by a universal scalar parameter, Gilbert damping can exhibit spatial dependence and tensorial characteristics determined by the underlying microscopic interactions.

papers.title_en: Finite Nonsignalling Resources Suffice to Simulate Entangled Qubits
papers.abstract_en: A longstanding question in Bell nonlocality is whether finite-alphabet nonsignalling resources can reproduce the continuum of measurement correlations of partially entangled qubits. Here we resolve this problem by showing that every fixed pure two-qubit state admits an exact simulation of all local projective-measurement statistics using shared randomness and finitely many Popescu-Rohrlich (PR) boxes, without communication or postselection. The boxes operate in parallel, with a worst-case bound independent of the measurement settings: at most $128\cot^4θ$ calls for the Schmidt state $\cosθ|00\rangle+\sinθ|11\rangle$, $0<θ<π/4$. The key is an exact finite-selection method that reduces input-dependent continuous sampling to a choice from a fixed-length shared random list, implemented through a finite PR-box network. The construction extends to arbitrary mixed two-qubit states and local binary-outcome POVMs. This reveals a fundamental separation between the continuity of quantum measurement correlations and the alphabet size of the resources needed to simulate them, shedding light on the resource-theoretic structure of Bell nonlocality.

papers.title_en: Quantum Evolution Networks Learn Long-Time Coherent Dynamics in Driven Spin Registers
papers.abstract_en: Predicting and controlling driven quantum systems requires access to dynamics across physical parameters, initial states, and evolution times. A reusable neural model must capture this dependence while preserving unitary structure and maintaining accuracy over long-time coherent evolution. Here we introduce Quantum Evolution Networks (QENs), which map physical parameters and time to complete propagators for periodically driven three-spin registers. Shared networks learn unitary one-period propagators and compatible within-period paths, enabling predictions through known periodic composition without query-specific numerical integration. For transverse driving, the fifth-percentile fidelity, minimized over input states and sampled times, is 0.9947 over 24 periods on 256 held-out configurations. A leading-order analysis of spectrally resolved endpoint residuals predicts multicycle process error more accurately than quadratic or spectrum-averaged estimates. Interventions at matched single-period infidelity produce orders-of-magnitude differences in multicycle infidelity, demonstrating the importance of residual orientation. Compatible component replacements identify how endpoint and within-period approximations limit reconstruction accuracy. These results establish a reusable neural representation of the studied propagator families and connect its learned residual structure to its observed long-time reliability.

papers.title_en: Photon-Number Discrimination from Increasing Time-of-Arrival Separation in Wide Superconducting Microstrip Single-Photon Detectors
papers.abstract_en: Measurements of photon-number-dependent time-of-arrival (TOA) distributions in wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors (SMSPDs) are presented. Two \SI{10}{\um}-long devices with widths of \SI{3.2}{\um} and \SI{6.4}{\um} are characterized under pulsed \SI{515}{nm} excitation. The TOA histograms are described by sums of exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) components, with the wider device exhibiting components assigned to photon numbers up to \(n=8\). Adjacent TOA peaks become more distinguishable relative to their widths at higher photon number, in contrast to the compression of neighboring photon-number timing shifts observed in conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs. For the components assigned to \(n=7\) and \(n=8\), the FWHM-normalized peak separation is \(2.15\), and the fitted EMG distributions yield an equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity of \(99.6\%\). The EMG exponential-tail parameter \(τ_n\) decreases strongly with photon number, while the Gaussian-location parameter \(μ_n\) continues to shift between neighboring components. A phenomenological model motivated by absorption-site-dependent vortex processes and collective current redistribution captures these timing trends. These results support wide SMSPDs as a platform for TOA-based photon-number discrimination at high photon number, relevant to multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing. The same geometry also provides a setting to examine how the spatial distribution of photon absorption affects vortex-assisted detection.

papers.title_en: Quantum Cryptomania with Classical Communication without One-Way Functions
papers.abstract_en: In classical cryptography, one-way functions are necessary for most of cryptography. In the quantum world, however, Kretschmer at {TQC'21} and subsequent works have demonstrated that quantum versions of various primitives in minicrypt, such as signatures and private-key encryption, do not require quantum-computable one-way functions (\textsf{qOWF}s). However, the question of the necessity of \textsf{qOWF}s for primitives in Cryptomania like public-key encryption with classical public keys and ciphertexts (\textsf{qPKE}) has remained open. We provide a comprehensive picture of the relationship between \textsf{qPKE} and \textsf{qOWF}. First, our main result is a black-box separation between \textsf{qOWF}s and \textsf{qPKE}. In particular, we show that relative to a unitary, real, and self-inverse oracle, there exists a \textsf{qPKE} scheme (with classical keys and ciphertexts), but \textsf{qOWF}s do not exist. Further, our oracles admit a point-function obfuscation construction, thus ruling out black-box construction of \textsf{qOWF} from point function obfuscations. On the positive side, we construct \textsf{qPKE} from quantum indistinguishability obfuscation for quantum circuits with classical obfuscated descriptions and efficiently verifiable one-way puzzles, which is known to be a potentially weaker assumption than \textsf{qOWF}s, due to an existing black-box separation. Our construction is the quantum analog of the classical construction of \textsf{PKE} from one-way functions and indistinguishability obfuscation in the quantum computation with classical communication (QCCC) setting.

papers.title_en: Coupled-channel extension of the effective-range expansion with left-hand cut
papers.abstract_en: We generalize the recently proposed effective-range expansion with a left-hand cut [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 011903 (2025)] to a coupled-channel framework. By systematically analyzing the singularity structure of the $S$-wave coupled-channel one-particle exchange (OPE) potential under various mass configurations, we derive an analytical parametrization of the coupled-channel scattering amplitude that incorporates the OPE left-hand cut for multiple channels. Taking the two-channel case as an illustration, we benchmark this parametrization against the Lippmann--Schwinger equation (LSE) by comparing the amplitudes and their inverses at different expansion orders. Even at the lowest order, with only six parameters, the coupled-channel parametrization faithfully reproduces the LSE results and enables precise extraction of the coupling constants, demonstrating its reliability for two-body coupled-channel scattering problems involving particle exchange.

papers.title_en: LYNX - A trapped-ion quantum information processor
papers.abstract_en: We introduce LYNX, a quantum information processor based on trapped $^{40}$Ca$^+$ ions. It utilizes up to 31 qubits with all-to-all connectivity. We characterize the system performance using rigorous benchmarks, such as randomized benchmarking (RB), GHZ state fidelity estimates, and quantum volume (QV) tests. The LYNX processor shows average 1-qubit gate errors of $8(5)\times 10^{-5}$ tested via standard RB in a 24-qubit register. An average 2-qubit gate error in a 24-qubit register of $2.84(8)\times 10^{-3}$ is demonstrated using interleaved RB. Furthermore, the device passes QV tests using up to 15 qubits which corresponds to a quantum volume of QV$=2^{15}$.

papers.title_en: Fundamental bound on Wigner negativity generation from environmental collisions
papers.abstract_en: Beyond quadratic potentials, classical evolution laws are typically thought to arise from quantum theory as an approximate description. Here we show that classical evolution laws can emerge exactly, provided the environment interacts with the system via collisions. We use this to derive an inequality that lower bounds the distribution of environmental momentum kicks by the absolute value of the Fourier transform of the potential. We show that violating this inequality is necessary and sufficient for a non-quadratic potential to generate negativity from the set of positive Wigner functions. A simple consequence of this is a lower bound on the heating rate for a quantum system to evolve effectively classically. We illustrate our results using the theory of a levitated nanoparticle subject to photon recoil and background gas collisions. We derive the strength of external potential needed to generate Wigner negative states in an optical tweezer and propose an experimental test of whether a nanoparticle in an optical lattice is operating in a non-classical regime.

papers.title_en: Orientational average in nuclear shape imaging: densities, correlations, and eccentricity in Ne-20
papers.abstract_en: The orientational treatment of deformed nuclei in high-energy nuclear collisions have two ways, a rigid rotor and a wave-function rotor, in which nuclear densities in laboratory frame are constructed differently. We calculate the one- and two-body densities (including Pauli blocking effects), body-axis contour multipoles, and geometric eccentricity variances under a leading-order ultracentral mapping for Ne-20 in a deformed harmonic-oscillator model in the rigid and wave-function rotors. At fixed deformation parameter $κ$ in the model, the two constructions can give different laboratory radial moments and pair correlations. The body-axis transition-kernel contours in the wave-function rotor are generally more compact along the symmetry axis, and $β_{20}$, $β_{40}$, $\langle\varepsilon_2^2\rangle$ and $\langle\varepsilon_4^2\rangle$ lie below the rigid-rotor results in a wide range of $κ$. The relations among these quantities in each rotor are nevertheless similar in most scanned parameter space: $β_{40}$ and $\langle\varepsilon_2^2\rangle$ depend linearly on $β_{20}^{2}$, while the hexadecapole baseline-subtracted variance follows an approximate quadratic trend in the quadrupole one. The method can be extended to seek more sensitive quantities for rotational effects in the wave-function rotor.

papers.title_en: Photon-Pair Advantage for Dissipative Parameter Estimation in Whispering-Gallery-Mode Interferometers
papers.abstract_en: We study the estimation of detuning and intrinsic loss in a lossy whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) resonator located in a balanced Mach--Zehnder interferometer. We use indistinguishable photon pairs and coherent-state probes. We show that using indistinguishable photon pairs can provide higher Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) of dissipative parameters, such as intrinsic loss, at resonance away from critical coupling. Taking into account all photon-loss outcomes, we obtain analytical QFI expressions and compare photon-pair and coherent-state probe results when they have the same mean photon number. For estimating the round-trip amplitude transmission at resonance and away from critical coupling, the photon-pair probe gives a higher QFI than the coherent-state probe, and photon-number-resolved detection saturates this QFI. This advantage is due to the photon-loss statistics and it is still accessible for a typical overcoupled condition after averaging over fluctuations of the unresolved detuning. We identify the limits of this advantage: phase doubling does not improve resonant detuning estimation, and coincidence-only detection is inefficient close to a zero transmission. These results identify the cases in which photon pairs can be useful for absorption and pump--probe WGM sensing.

papers.title_en: Two-Layer Verification for Fault-Tolerant Magic-State Preparation in High-Rate Quantum Codes
papers.abstract_en: Encoded magic states are essential for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation, but their resource-efficient preparation in high-rate quantum codes remains challenging. To address this limitation, we propose two-layer verification, which combines local verification of independently prepared subblocks with logical verification after their embedding into a target code. This hierarchy detects harmful error patterns, including even-parity logical-eigenvalue flips that are invisible to a collective product check alone. We demonstrate this scheme for a $[[21,3,5]]$ code by constructing a circuit that embeds three verified seven-qubit Steane-code magic states into the target code. Circuit-level simulations of $T$- and $S$-state preparation show logical-error suppression consistent with the code distance. These results demonstrate the potential of two-layer verification as a design principle for reliable magic-state preparation in quantum codes encoding multiple logical qubits.

papers.title_en: Electron Wavefronts Capture Nanoscale Movies of Hypersound at Surfaces
papers.abstract_en: Acoustic waves transport mechanical energy and elastic strain through solids, with material composition and shape governing their propagation. In the gigahertz hypersound regime, acoustic wavelengths reach tens to hundreds of nanometres, comparable to nanoscale device dimensions. Harnessing these waves underpins high-frequency signal processing, sensing, electromagnetic coupling and quantum control. Acoustic metrology probes elastic modes and internal interfaces. Yet directly imaging how nanoscale acoustic waves interact with local structure remains challenging, requiring picometre displacement sensitivity combined with high spatiotemporal resolution. Here we demonstrate full-field imaging of laser-induced hypersound at surfaces using reflected electron wavefronts. We introduce ultrafast low-energy electron microscopy (ULEEM), exploiting the intrinsic surface sensitivity of few-electronvolt electrons. Coherent electron pulses down to femtosecond durations reflect from the topmost atomic layers, imprinting the evolving surface profile onto their wavefronts. Defocus converts phase variations into image contrast. In a thin van der Waals material, we image the thermoelastic generation and propagation of picometre-amplitude acoustic waves. Measured dispersion relations, interpreted through elastodynamic modelling, distinguish substrate-supported and locally detached regions, revealing how interfacial contact shapes propagation. Delayed wave emission reveals scattering at buried mechanical defects. Our results establish electron-wavefront imaging of nanoscale surface dynamics, enabling the exploration of ultrafast energy transport, structural transformations and coupled mechanical, electronic and magnetic phenomena.

papers.title_en: Trident: Efficient Load Verification for Yoked Surface Codes using a Three-Level Memory Hierarchy
papers.abstract_en: Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers (FTQCs) commonly use the surface code to encode program qubits as error-corrected logical qubits. Unfortunately, the surface code has a poor encoding rate, so recent work has proposed Yoked Surface Codes (YSCs), which concatenate the surface code with a high-rate quantum code. The surface code qubits in YSCs are protected by the checks, or yokes, of the high-rate code. YSCs have 1D and 2D variants, which are $1.8\times$ and $4.5\times$ more efficient than the surface code, respectively. Modern FTQC architectures use a two-level hierarchy: surface codes perform logical operations (compute) while 2D YSCs store idle program qubits (memory).
